chunks.heading: AI and your privacy — What is AI?
chunks.text:
AI programs learn from information you give them, so it is important to only share safe details and keep your personal secrets private.

AI (Artificial Intelligence) is like a very smart robot inside your computer or phone. It learns by looking at lots of information. When you ask it a question, it uses what it has learned to give you an answer.

chunks.heading: How Does AI See My Information? — Why Does This Matter for My Privacy?
chunks.text:
When you type a question to an AI program, it reads what you wrote. Some companies that make these AI programs might save what you type so the robot can learn even more for the next person.

Privacy means keeping your personal life a secret from strangers. If you tell the AI your bank password, your home address, or a secret about your family, that information might be saved by the company. We do not want our secrets to be saved where strangers might see them.

chunks.heading: How to Keep Your Secrets Safe
chunks.text: 1. Do not share passwords: Never tell an AI program your passwords. 2. Do not share bank details: Keep your money safe by not typing your card numbers into AI tools. 3. Do not share personal secrets: If you wouldn't tell a stranger on the street, do not tell the AI.

chunks.heading: The Golden Rule
chunks.text: Think of AI like a helpful stranger. You can ask it to help you write a letter or find a recipe, but never share your private information with it.

chunks.heading: AI detecting online scams — What Is an Online Scam?
chunks.text:
Learn how smart computer programs can help spot and stop bad people from tricking you on the internet.

An online scam is when someone tries to trick you on the internet. They might: - Send you a fake message asking for your money - Pretend to be someone they are not - Make a fake website that looks real - Promise you something that is too good to be true These bad people want to steal your money or your personal information.

chunks.heading: What Are Smart Computer Programs?
chunks.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is when computers are taught to think and learn like humans. They can: - Look at lots of information very fast - Find patterns that humans might miss - Learn from mistakes to get better over time - Watch for bad things happening online Think of it like having a very clever guard dog that never sleeps and can watch many doors at the same time.

chunks.heading: How Do These Programs Find Scams? — 1. Strange Messages
chunks.text:
These smart programs look for signs that something might be a scam:

The program checks messages for words and phrases that scammers often use. If a message says "You won a prize!" or "Send money now!", the program might flag it.

chunks.heading: 2. Fake Websites — 3. Bad Behaviour
chunks.text:
The program can check if a website is pretending to be a real bank or shop. It looks for small differences that humans might not notice.

If someone sends thousands of messages very fast, the program might think this is a scammer, not a real person.

chunks.heading: 4. Unusual Requests — How Does This Help You?
chunks.text:
If someone you don't know asks for your bank details or password, the program can warn you this might be dangerous.

When you use the internet, these smart programs are often working in the background to keep you safe: - Your email might move suspicious messages to a "spam" folder - Your bank might text you if someone tries to use your card in a strange way - Your phone might warn you if a website is dangerous - Your messages app might tell you if a link looks suspicious These warnings are there to help you stop and think before you do something you might regret.

chunks.heading: What Should You Still Watch Out For?
chunks.text: Even with smart programs helping, you still need to be careful: 1. Be suspicious of urgent requests - Real banks and companies don't ask you to act immediately 2. Check website addresses carefully - Scammers make addresses that look almost right 3. Never share passwords - No real company will ask for your password 4. Ask someone you trust - If something feels wrong, ask a family member or friend

chunks.heading: Remember
chunks.text: Smart computer programs help protect you, but they are not perfect. You are still the best protector of yourself. When something feels wrong, trust your feelings and ask for help. If you think someone has tried to scam you, tell someone you trust right away. You can also report scams to help protect others.

chunks.heading: Free AI tools for beginners — Free tools to try
chunks.text:
You will learn how to use free artificial intelligence tools for simple tasks like writing, learning, and finding ideas.

Artificial intelligence tools are computer helpers. You can ask them to write, explain, translate, or suggest ideas.

- ChatGPT — Ask questions, write messages, or explain difficult words. - Google Gemini — Ask questions and get help with learning or planning. - Microsoft Copilot — Ask for writing help, ideas, or simple explanations. - Canva — Make simple posters, cards, and pictures. Some features are free.

chunks.heading: How to use one — Important safety tips
chunks.text:
1. Open the tool’s website. 2. Type what you need in the message box. 3. Use simple words, such as: “Explain this letter in easy English.” 4. Read the answer carefully. 5. Ask again if you do not understand.

- Do not share your password, bank details, or private identity number. - Do not believe every answer. The tool can make mistakes. - Check important information with a trusted person or website. - Free tools may offer paid features. Do not enter payment details unless you want to pay. - Be careful when downloading files or clicking links.

chunks.heading: Useful things to ask
chunks.text: - “Write a polite message to my landlord.” - “Translate this into simple English.” - “Give me a shopping list for five cheap meals.” - “Explain this health letter in easy words.” - “Help me practise a job interview.”

chunks.heading: How phones use AI
chunks.text:
You will learn how phones use smart computer tools to understand words, pictures, sounds, and your habits.

Artificial intelligence means a computer doing tasks that usually need human thinking. Phones use it in many simple ways: - Voice help: Your phone listens to your words and turns them into text or follows a command. - Better typing: It guesses the next word while you write a message. - Photo help: It can find faces, pets, food, or places in your pictures. - Maps: It can suggest a quicker road and warn about traffic. - Safety: It can notice unwanted calls or suspicious messages. - Translation: It can change words from one language to another. - Personal suggestions: It may suggest music, videos, or news you might like. The phone learns from examples and patterns. It does not think or feel like a person. It can make mistakes, so check important information. You can help protect yourself by: - Checking what the phone is allowed to see or hear. - Avoiding sharing private information with unknown apps. - Asking a trusted person when something seems strange.

chunks.heading: Staying Safe When Using AI
chunks.text:
Learn how to use computer helpers safely by protecting your private information and knowing that they can make mistakes.

AI (Artificial Intelligence) is like a very smart computer program that can talk to you, write things, or make pictures. You might use it on your phone or computer to ask questions or get help. While it is a helpful tool, we must be careful, just like when we cross the street or talk to strangers. Here is how you can stay safe:

chunks.heading: 1. Keep Your Secrets Safe
chunks.text: Never tell the computer helper your private information. This includes your bank account numbers, passwords, home address, or phone number. Think of the computer helper like a stranger on the bus. You wouldn't tell a stranger your secret money hiding spot!

chunks.heading: 2. Computers Can Make Mistakes
chunks.text: AI is smart, but it does not know everything. Sometimes, it might tell you something that is not true. If you need important advice about your health or your money, always ask a real doctor or a trusted family member. Do not trust the computer completely.

chunks.heading: 3. Watch Out for Fake Voices and Videos
chunks.text: Bad people can use AI to copy the voice of someone you know, like your grandchild. They might call you on the phone and ask for money, sounding just like them. If someone calls asking for money in a strange way, hang up and call them back on a phone number you know is real.

chunks.heading: 4. Be the Boss
chunks.text: You are in charge. If the computer helper says something that feels wrong or makes you uncomfortable, you can stop using it or ask it to change the subject. You do not have to do what it says. By following these simple steps, you can enjoy using new computer helpers without worry!

chunks.heading: Using AI to Read Documents — What can it do?
chunks.text:
You will learn how to use an artificial intelligence tool to understand, summarise, and find information in documents.

Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a computer helper. It can look at a document and explain it in simple words.

An AI tool may help you: - Read a letter or notice - Make a long document shorter - Explain difficult words - Find a name, date, price, or address - Translate a document - Answer questions about the document

chunks.heading: How to use it
chunks.text: 1. Open an AI app or website. 2. Choose Add file, Upload, or the camera picture button. 3. Take a clear picture of the document, or choose a saved file. 4. Ask a simple question, such as: - “Please explain this in simple words.” - “What date must I remember?” - “How much money does this say?” 5. Read the answer carefully.

chunks.heading: Stay safe
chunks.text: - Do not upload passwords, bank details, identity numbers, or private medical papers unless you trust the service. - Check important information with the original document. - AI can make mistakes. Ask a trusted person or office if something is unclear. - Make sure the picture shows the whole page and is not blurry.

chunks.heading: Using AI to Translate Languages
chunks.text:
Learn how smart computer programs can change your words into another language so you can talk to more people.

Have you ever wanted to talk to someone who speaks a different language? Maybe you have a doctor or a neighbor who does not understand your words. Now, computers can help you talk to them easily.

chunks.heading: What is Computer Translation?
chunks.text: Think of your phone or computer as a very smart friend who knows many languages. When you speak or type words, this friend quickly tells you what those words mean in another language. In the past, computers were not very good at this and made silly mistakes. Today, they are very smart and can change whole sentences so they make sense.

chunks.heading: How Can You Use It?
chunks.text: You can use your phone to change languages in a few simple ways: 1. Talking to people: You can speak into your phone in your language. The phone will then speak the same words out loud in the other language. The other person can reply, and your phone will change their words back to your language. 2. Reading signs or papers: If you get a letter in a language you do not know, you can take a picture of it with your phone. The phone will change the words in the picture to your language so you can read it. 3. Shopping online: If a website is in a different language, the computer can change the whole page to your language so you can understand what you are buying.

chunks.heading: Where to Find This Tool
chunks.text: One of the most famous tools for this is called Google Translate. It is free to use. You just need an internet connection on your phone or computer. You can also download apps on your phone that do the same thing. Using these tools makes the world smaller. You do not need to feel scared or left out when you see or hear words you do not know. Your phone can be your helpful translator friend!

chunks.heading: Using AI to write messages — How to use it
chunks.text:
You will learn how to ask artificial intelligence to help write clear messages and check them before sending.

Artificial intelligence can help you write a message. It is like a writing helper on your phone or computer.

1. Open an artificial intelligence writing tool. 2. Tell it what you want to say. 3. Say who the message is for and what feeling you want. For example: > Write a short, friendly message to my doctor. Say that I cannot come to my appointment tomorrow and ask for a new date. The tool may write: > Hello Doctor, I cannot come to my appointment tomorrow. Could I please have a new date? Thank you.

chunks.heading: Check the message
chunks.text: Before sending: - Read the whole message. - Make sure the details are correct. - Change any words that do not sound like you. - Check the person’s name and date. - Send it only when you are happy with it.

chunks.heading: Keep private things safe
chunks.text: Do not type private information into a writing tool, such as: - Passwords - Bank details - Identity numbers - Private medical information Artificial intelligence can make mistakes. You are the person who must check the message before sending it.
